title: Exploring the Paranormal Unknown / Open Lines
excerpt: Filmmaker Paul Davids explored UFO disclosure, ancient mysteries, government disinformation, AI, and communication after death. Open Lines followed in the latter half of the program.
content:
About the show

Guest host Rich Berra (email) welcomed filmmaker Paul Davids, who discussed his transformation from a skeptic into a believer in UFOs and paranormal phenomena, beginning with a daylight UFO sighting in 1987. Reflecting on recent visits to Machu Picchu, Sacsayhuamán, and Easter Island, he questioned how ancient civilizations constructed massive stone structures without advanced technology. Davids speculated that extraterrestrial civilizations possessing anti-gravity technology may have influenced humanity's early development.

Davids argued that the government has deliberately concealed evidence of extraterrestrial visitation since the 1947 Roswell incident. Citing Jay Stratton's book Out of the Shadows, he described a longstanding campaign of disinformation designed to suppress UFO research and discourage public acceptance. Comparing this secrecy to the Catholic Church's historical rejection of Galileo's discoveries, he maintained that disclosure is essential for scientific progress. He also expressed concern about artificial intelligence, its unpredictable capabilities, and the growing difficulty of distinguishing authentic information from fabricated content.

Turning to life after death, Davids recounted unexplained experiences following the death of his mentor, Forrest J. Ackerman, which convinced him that spirit communication is possible. He described experimenting with AI-generated video of a deceased childhood friend in hopes of initiating contact, followed by unexplained appearances of old photographs on his devices. Davids also recalled electrical disturbances during a screening of his Life After Death Project documentary and a psychic's apparent success in locating murder victims. He emphasized that spirit communication generally seems to originate from the deceased rather than the living.

------------------------------------------

During Open Lines, Jerry in Hemet, California, described an extraordinary experience during a gathering with spiritual teacher Robert Adams in the Hollywood Hills. He claimed to have seen rotating spirals in Adams' eyes before experiencing what seemed like an out-of-body encounter in which he floated toward the guru. Frightened by the intensity of the experience, he said he withdrew and immediately found himself back in his chair. Jerry explained Adams' philosophy that physical existence is an illusion and consciousness represents our true nature. He also recalled driving across the Mojave Desert with a broken water pump, believing his vehicle's unexplained survival demonstrated that reality can sometimes transcend physical limitations.

Mike from Phoenix, Arizona, discussed ancient spiritual traditions and unconventional theories about the universe's origins. He suggested that Jesus may have traveled to India during the undocumented years of his life and studied Hindu teachings. He also referenced Hindu beliefs about multiple Big Bangs and previous realities, suggesting that ancient traditions preserve knowledge predating written history. Turning to the Moon, Mike claimed that Native American legends describe a time before its arrival and speculated that a spacecraft transported it to Earth. He further asserted that the Moon is hollow and inhabited by approximately 50,000 people.

Mark in Ventura, California, challenged Paul Davids' discussion of Galileo by emphasizing that Nicolaus Copernicus had advanced the heliocentric model decades earlier. He then argued that government intelligence agencies deliberately spread misinformation to manipulate the public through fear, citing an alleged statement by former CIA Director William Casey. Mark also questioned the official account of President Kennedy's assassination and criticized the lack of attention given to the 1967 USS Liberty incident. Distrustful of modern media and technology, he said he avoids television, smartphones, and the internet, relying instead on books and traditional encyclopedias for information.
